newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPALS -- up slightly amid new issues.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPALS -- up slightly amid new issues.

text.p: The U.S. municipal market was unchanged to up about 1/8 point by midday Tuesday, as several of the week's new deals priced, traders said.
Secondary market activity was quiet, with most of the action centered on more than $1 billion of new issues set for pricing.

Prudential Securities won Tuesday's largest competitive offering, a $215 million Minnesota general obligation deal. The firm reoffered the 2017 maturity at a 5.15 percent yield. To see the reoffering scale, double click on nN29152684.

In the negotiated sector, Banc One Capital Corp said it tentatively priced $100 million Texas Water Development Board bonds at a top yield of 5.25 percent in 2020. To see the preliminary pricing, double click on nN29297592.
Tuesday's new issues were expected to total $1.1 billion in 40 sales, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.
The main data released Tuesday, the second quarter Employment Cost Index, showed an overall 0.8 percent rise, which was in line with the increase forecast by economists.
Treasury prices initially dipped after the data, but recovered in later trade. The long bond was up 3/32 at 103, pushing the yield down to 6.40 percent.

Despite that gain, analysts said investors were nervous about the next big indicator -- Friday's jobs report for July. Economist surveyed by Reuters on average expected non-farm payrolls to show a 193,000 gain, and the unemployment rate to have dropped to 4.9 percent from 5.0 percent in June.

At midday Tuesday, September municipal bond futures rose 9/32 to 121-10/32, while Treasury bond futures gained 8/32 to 115-22/32. The MOB spread between the two contracts widened to 180 ticks from 179 at the close Monday.
Actively quoted bonds in the muni secondary market included Harris County, Texas, Toll Road MBIA 5.0s of 2024. Bids dropped two basis points to 5.31 percent.
Florida Ports Financing Commission MBIA 5-3/8s of 2027 were bid at 5.48 percent, down one basis point.
